strategies.summary: Map the current price leg from its origin swing low to its confirmed swing high, then mark the first retracement PD array as the first line of defense. The higher-probability case is a bullish FVG overlapping a bullish order block, while the origin swing low is the last line of defense.

timeframes.notes: Fractal concept. setup_tf is the leg timeframe being analysed; bearish examples are mirrored through the catalog mirror table.

glossary.First line of defense: FLOD (older spelling FLOT): the first PD array met on the retracement; in this lesson the higher-probability case is an FVG overlapping an order block, via custom_signals.flod and custom_signals.overlapping_pd_array.
glossary.Last line of defense: LLOD (older spelling LOT): the swing extreme at the origin of the current leg; see custom_signals.llod.
glossary.Price action leg: The swing low-to-swing high range being retraced; the transcript also says 'price action lag'.

custom_signals.name: flod
custom_signals.plain_definition: First line of defense: the first PD array met on a retracement, most often a fair value gap.

custom_signals.name: llod
custom_signals.plain_definition: Last line of defense: the swing extreme at the origin of the current price leg.

custom_signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: A fair value gap that shares price with another PD array (order block) on the same timeframe; the shared range is the entry zone.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: max(bullish_fvg[0].gap_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(bullish_fvg[0].gap_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated

sequence: Mark the current bullish price leg from its origin swing low to the confirmed swing high that created the retracement.
Scan the retracement path for a bullish fair value gap and a bullish order block that share price.
Treat that overlap as the first line of defense on the retracement.
If price closes below the origin swing low, the leg has failed and a new opposite leg must be mapped.

invalidation.text: Price breaks and stays beyond the Last Line of Defense (the swing extreme), creating a new opposite price action leg.

filters.text: Avoid taking setups off isolated fair value gaps. The probabilities are significantly higher when the FVG overlaps with another PD array.

stop_rule.text: For the bullish reading, price should not stay below the leg's origin swing low (the last line of defense).
stop_rule.quote: we shouldn't stay below that low

presenter_claims.claim: The first line of defense holding is usually 9 out of 10 times an overlapping pattern, primarily a fair value gap.
High probability conditions (overlapping arrays) have an 80% win rate, while low probability conditions have a 20% win rate.

strategies.notes: Framework, not a standalone entry model: it explains how to rank PD arrays inside a retracement. The higher-probability case is the overlap of a bullish FVG and a bullish order block. Written on the canonical bullish side; the presenter examples are bearish mirrors.
